known_limitations: the core team operated every role: the owner, the coordinator and the two model clients
the confirmers were harness-driven: the real confirmers on pseudo-terminals the custody accounts opened, typing the code only for the action or purchase the model's own tool result named
init of each provider and buyer node was harness-driven in the custody accounts
every endpoint is a local validator of this host
one developer account ran both clients, not two (owner ruling)
the paid request pending across the switch was held by stopping the provider agent, not by load

Codex 0.171 still lists, with its shell and file tools disabled and a read-only sandbox, its code-mode exec (the host through which it calls MCP tools), apply_patch and its collaboration tools; no session used them. The tool-use check is not live: after each session exits, the driver reads its transcript (unexpected_tools) and cmd_step then stops the assignment on any tool use outside the role's MCP server (check above)

the developer account is the operator account and has sudo (owner ruling: the clients already logged in there were used); the clients had no shell or file tool, so the model could not use sudo (Codex still listed the tools named in the item above)

the operator's home, which is the developer account's, holds 967 OpenFox files from earlier work; no run process executed, read or had on its PATH any of them (the clients had no shell or file tool), and openfox_absent covers every binary, installed directory, custody home and the run's PATH
